title: Statistics - Lesson 8: Percentile Rank Assessment
description: Assessment for calculating, comparing, and interpreting percentile rank.

questions.question: Which formula matches the below-score convention for percentile rank?
options: (number of values below the score / total number of values) x 100
(total number of values / number of values below the score) x 100
questions.explanation: The below-score convention compares the number of values below the target score with the total number of values.

questions.question: Order is not required in your answer. In the data set 72, 65, 80, 58, 74, how many values are below 74? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The values below 74 are 72, 65, and 58, so the correct count is 3.

questions.question: In the ordered data set 55, 60, 66, 71, 77, 84, 90, 95, what is the percentile rank of 77 using the below-score convention?
questions.explanation: Four of the eight values are below 77, so (4/8) x 100 = 50.

questions.question: The 90th percentile means the score is exactly 90% correct.
questions.explanation: Percentile rank describes relative standing in a data set, not the percent correct on an assignment.

questions.question: A score has 18 values below it in a data set of 30 values. Which percentile rank is correct?
questions.explanation: (18/30) x 100 = 60, so the score is at the 60th percentile.

questions.question: Use the ordered data set 31, 35, 39, 42, 46, 50, 54, 58, 62, 66. What is the percentile rank of 54 using the at-or-below convention?
questions.explanation: At-or-below counts 31, 35, 39, 42, 46, 50, and 54. That is 7 out of 10, so the rank is 70.

questions.question: A score has 11 values below it out of 20 total values. What is the percentile rank? Enter the percent without the percent sign.
questions.explanation: (11/20) x 100 = 55, so the score is at the 55th percentile.

questions.question: Which interpretation is strongest for this result: Maya's typing speed is at the 85th percentile among 40 students?
options: Maya's typing speed is higher than about 85% of the typing speeds in this group of 40 students.
Maya is better than everyone in the school.
questions.explanation: The strongest interpretation connects the percentile rank to the comparison group and avoids overclaiming.

questions.question: If a problem says to use the below-score convention, you should not count the target score itself.
questions.explanation: Below-score means strictly less than the target score.

questions.question: A data set has 12 values. A target score is the 9th value in the ordered list, and all values are different. Using the below-score convention, what is its percentile rank?
questions.explanation: If the target is the 9th value, then 8 values are below it. (8/12) x 100 = 66.7, which rounds to the 67th percentile.

questions.question: Use the below-score convention. In the ordered data set 44, 49, 53, 59, 63, 68, 72, 77, find and interpret the percentile rank of 63.
questions.correctAnswer: Four of the eight values are below 63, so (4/8) x 100 = 50. The score 63 is higher than 50% of the values in the data set.
questions.explanation: The answer should include the count below, the computation, and a sentence explaining the relative standing.

questions.question: A learner says, "My score is at the 70th percentile, so I got 70 points." Explain why this may be wrong.
questions.correctAnswer: Percentile rank is not the raw score. It means the learner's score is higher than about 70% of the scores in the comparison group.
questions.explanation: This response corrects the common confusion between a score and a percentile rank.

questions.question: Use the ordered data set 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26, 29, 32. Which score is at the 40th percentile using the below-score convention?
questions.explanation: The 40th percentile means 40% of 10 values, or 4 values, are below the target. The score with four values below it is 17.

questions.question: A score of 76 has 15 scores below it in a set of 24 scores. Find the percentile rank to the nearest whole percentile and interpret it.
questions.correctAnswer: (15/24) x 100 = 62.5, which rounds to the 63rd percentile. A score of 76 is higher than about 63% of the scores in the data set.
questions.explanation: The computation gives 62.5, and rounding to the nearest whole percentile gives 63. The interpretation must mention relative standing.

questions.question: Which mistake would most likely make a percentile rank too high?
options: Counting values above the score as if they were below it
Ordering the data from least to greatest
Dividing by the total number of values
questions.explanation: Including values above the target score in the count below would inflate the numerator and make the percentile rank too high.
